body:
For example, what if we just check the main branch and conduct some focused reviews? 

@sepo-agent

comments.body:
Yes, this is feasible, but it is not just a one-line router change. Today `/review` is intentionally PR-only:

- Dispatch prompt says `review` is only valid for `pull_request`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/agent-dispatch.md#L10-L17
- `applyDispatchPolicy` rejects review requests unless `targetKind === "pull_request"`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.agent/src/triage.ts#L446-L457
- `agent-router.yml` only calls `agent-review.yml` when the target is a PR: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-router.yml#L1116-L1132
- `agent-review.yml` requires `pr_number` and passes `target_kind: pull_request` into reviewer and synthesis runs: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L3-L42 and https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/workflows/agent-review.yml#L220-L225
- The review prompt is diff-centered and tells reviewers to use `gh pr diff`: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/blob/main/.github/prompts/review.md#L3-L12

I’d implement this as an **issue-scoped focused review mode** under the existing `review` route, keeping PR review behavior unchanged.

Plan:

1. Allow `review` on `issue` and `pull_request` in `.agent/src/triage.ts`; still reject discussions/other targets. Update triage tests that currently assert review-on-issue is unsupported.

2. Update `.github/workflows/agent-router.yml` so the review job can dispatch for issue targets too, passing `target_kind` and `target_number` instead of only `pr_number`.

3. Refactor `.github/workflows/agent-review.yml` to accept:
   - `target_kind`
   - `target_number`
   - legacy `pr_number` for workflow_dispatch compatibility

   For PRs, preserve the current path: capture PR head, run PR diff review, rubrics review, synthesis, PR comment.

   For issues, use the default branch checkout as the review subject, skip PR-head capture, skip inline PR comment management, and post the synthesis back to the issue.

4. Add or generalize prompts:
   - PR mode keeps using `gh pr view` / `gh pr diff`.
   - Issue mode reads the issue body/comments, checks out the default branch, derives a focused scope from the request, and reviews only that scope. If the issue does not contain enough scope, the review should say so instead of attempting a whole-repo audit.

5. Adjust synthesis so issue-mode review produces an issue-friendly summary and action items, with no PR inline-comment instructions.

6. Update docs in `README.md` and `.agent/docs/usage/supported-workflows.md` to say `/review` works on PRs for diff review and issues for focused default-branch review.

7. Add tests around:
   - explicit `@sepo-agent /review` on issue dispatches review
   - `agent/review` label on issue dispatches review
   - PR review route remains unchanged
   - issue review posts to issue comments and does not try PR-only inline operations

Recommended default behavior: issue `/review` should require or infer a focused scope from the issue/request. It should not silently do a whole-main-branch review unless the user explicitly asks for a broad audit.

Approve this direction and I can implement it.

---
`codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `Macmini-runner-1`
but for the review route in issues, can you make sure the user inline message is included such that it will have a clear goal for what to review for?

Implemented. Issue `/review` now carries the triggering inline message through as `request_text` plus source/comment metadata, and the review/synthesis prompts explicitly treat that text as the focused review goal for default-branch issue reviews.

Also updated routing so `review` is valid on issues and PRs, made `agent-review.yml` target-aware, posts issue review synthesis back to the issue, skips PR-only rubrics/head/inline behavior for issue targets, and updated docs/tests.

Verification:
- `npm --prefix .agent run build`
- `node --test .agent/dist/__tests__/triage.test.js .agent/dist/__tests__/envelope.test.js`
- `env -u GITHUB_OUTPUT npm --prefix .agent test` → 715 passed

`codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-5`

@sepo-agent /answer

Please investigate an inconsistency in the answer-route footer / template metadata. I expected these two Sepo answers to use the same answer template and display model metadata consistently:

- #396 initial issue mention answer: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/396#issuecomment-4606994467
  - run: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26847747552
  - footer: `codex` | `gpt-5.5/xhigh` | `Macmini-runner-1`
- #395 implicit follow-up answer: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/issues/395#issuecomment-4606983913
  - run: https://github.com/self-evolving/repo/actions/runs/26847712984
  - footer: `codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-5`

Questions:

1. Are both actually using `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`, or does the implicit follow-up path use a different answer template/context?
2. Why does one footer encode reasoning in the model (`gpt-5.5/xhigh`) while the other shows model and reasoning separately (`gpt-5.5` | `high`)?
3. Is this due to fresh vs resumed sessions, the `followup-intent` gate, or inconsistent reasoning-effort defaults between dispatch/answer paths?
4. If it is just display metadata, please propose how to normalize it so answer-route comments show the same footer shape across explicit and implicit follow-up runs.

No implementation needed yet; first please investigate and explain the root cause / recommended fix.

Context compacted
I checked the current workflow/code and the two run records. Both runs were on the same SHA (`7ef46d3...`) and both final posted comments went through the `agent / answer` job with `prompt: answer`, which maps to `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md`.

The implicit follow-up path does add one extra portal step first: `followup-intent`. That uses the follow-up intent prompt as a gate to decide `respond` vs `ignore`, but it is not the posted answer template.

The footer mismatch looks like display metadata, not template selection.

Current behavior:

- The final answer job uses `reasoning_effort: provider_output || 'high'`.
- `run.ts` prefers the ACP/Codex session-reported model over the requested model when building the footer.
- Codex GPT-5 reasoning can be encoded into the effective model ID, for example `gpt-5.5/xhigh`.
- If the reported model already contains `/high` or `/xhigh`, the footer suppresses the separate reasoning column.

So these two shapes can come from the same answer route:

```text
reported model: gpt-5.5/xhigh
footer: codex | gpt-5.5/xhigh | Macmini-runner-1

reported model: gpt-5.5
reasoning env: high
footer: codex | gpt-5.5 | high | Macmini-runner-5
```

That means the inconsistency is not caused by `.github/prompts/agent-answer.md` vs another answer template. It also is not directly caused by the `followup-intent` gate, because the final answer job reruns the answer provider and answer prompt afterward.

The likely root cause is that the footer currently mixes two metadata representations: sometimes reasoning is encoded in the Codex model string, and sometimes it is displayed from `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT`. Resumed answer sessions can make this more visible because the display trusts the session-reported model, but the bug is the footer normalization, not the existence of resumed sessions itself.

Recommended fix:

1. Normalize Codex model display before rendering the footer.
2. Parse effective model IDs like `gpt-5.5/xhigh` into:
   - model: `gpt-5.5`
   - reasoning: `xhigh`
3. Render one canonical answer footer shape for all answer-route comments.

I’d recommend the canonical shape remain:

```text
codex | gpt-5.5 | xhigh | runner
```

rather than:

```text
codex | gpt-5.5/xhigh | runner
```

because existing footer semantics already appear to be provider, model, reasoning, runner.

Implementation-wise, the clean change would be to update the model/footer helper so it decomposes Codex reasoning suffixes instead of only suppressing the reasoning column. Then add tests for:

- `gpt-5.5/xhigh` renders as `codex | gpt-5.5 | xhigh | runner`
- `gpt-5.5` plus `MODEL_REASONING_EFFORT=high` renders as `codex | gpt-5.5 | high | runner`
- non-Codex providers keep their current behavior.

---
`codex` | `gpt-5.5` | `high` | `Macmini-runner-3`
Closing because this agent issue has had no activity for 30 days.
